messages:
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chu <alex.chu@pulseiq.com>, procurement@pulseiq.com
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call debrief: decision roster, procurement path, and SLA exception request
Attachments: Requested-SLA-change-proposal.pdf (pdf stub)

Alex / PulseIQ team — thanks again for the 30-minute discovery earlier. Quick recap and asks so we keep momentum: 

Summary from our side
- Use case: triage-assist in clinician workflow (short-form generation + retrieval).
- Target scope: 5 seats for pilot, 3k messages/mo, expected peak concurrency in mornings.
- Key constraints: procurement requires an approved contract (MSA + SOW), security wants SOC2 evidence and clarity on audit logs, and legal flagged a 99.95% SLA ask for production.

Immediate asks (can you confirm):
1) Economic buyer / final signatory — you mentioned Dana Lopez (CFO). Confirm email and whether CFO will sign pilot MSA or only final contract.
2) Procurement route — is purchase via procurement@pulseiq.com or direct SOW? Any PO process/timing we should expect?
3) Security must-haves — you said SOC2 + field-level encryption + 90-day retention? Please confirm the retention window you need.

What we can offer now (internal ask to my team included below)
- Short pilot pricing: we can propose a pilot rate; Alex asked if a discount is possible. Typical pilot discount range we approve without exec sign-off is up to 15% for 30-day PoC. Anything deeper requires approval.
- SLA: production-level SLA (99.95%) would need legal review and Ops commit; for pilot we can offer best-effort with an operational schedule and incident reporting. If PulseIQ needs a formal SLA during pilot, we need an internal exception.

Next steps proposed
- Alex: share procurement contact and confirm Dana Lopez as economic buyer (and whether she’ll sign pilot).
- PulseIQ: confirm exact retention requirement and whether they need log exports for audits.
- Redwood internal: Laura / Dev / Marissa — can you confirm whether we can: (a) approve 20% pilot discount as a one-off, and (b) grant a pilot SLA exception (written) while legal finalizes MSA?

Thanks — I can set up an MAP once procurement path is clear.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call debrief: decision roster, procurement path, and SLA exception request

Ben — great summary, thanks. Quick answers: 
- Confirmed: Dana Lopez (CFO) is the economic buyer and will be the final signatory for commercial agreements over $25k. For a small pilot (under $10k) she has delegated sign-off to procurement.
- Procurement route: procurement@pulseiq.com handles PO and vendor onboarding. Expect an initial vendor questionnaire and a three-week review.
- Security requirements: SOC2 Type II report is a must; encryption at rest (AES-256) and TLS in transit; audit log exports for the pilot team for 30 days (they mentioned 30 days explicitly).

Regarding discount/SLA: the pilot budget is tight — Alex asks if you can do 20% off pilot pricing. For the SLA, they prefer a written commitment even for pilot to present to their security team (not necessarily a legal SLA, but an operational guarantee).

I can introduce you to procurement (I'll loop them in a separate thread if helpful).

—Alex
Alex Chu
Director of Platform Ops, PulseIQ
alex.chu@pulseiq.com

Ben — thanks for the note. A few internal points to keep in mind before we commit: 
1) Discount policy: standard autonomous pilot discount cap is 15% without leadership sign-off. Anything at 20%+ requires approval from Rishi (sales lead) and finance review. Please include expected pilot revenue amount in the ask.
2) SLA: granting a written SLA for pilot is unusual — legal will prefer a limited, non-binding operations statement. If PulseIQ insists on a contractual SLA during pilot, that needs legal + ops sign-off and we should expect to add indemnities.
3) Procurement cycles: procurement will require vendor questionnaires + security addenda; dev — can you list which artifacts we should prepare and whether we can provide a SOC2 attestation + temporary log export for 30 days?

I've attached a redline of our MSA with callouts where a pilot-specific clause can be inserted (see section 2.3 and 8.1).

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call debrief: decision roster, procurement path, and SLA exception request

Laura / Ben — technical input and list of artifacts we can commit quickly: 
- SOC2 Type II report: we can provide our latest attestation within 2 business days (PDF).
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit — standard.
- Audit/log exports: we can provide 30-day export to PulseIQ under an NDA; we do not persist PII beyond configured retention.
- Pilot SLA: for a 30-day pilot we recommend a "Pilot Operational Commitment" doc (non-contractual) that states: monitored availability target of 99% during pilot hours, SLA-level escalation path, and incident reporting cadence. For a contractual SLA (99.95% or greater) we need an ops runbook and capacity reservation — that would be an exception.

Proposed compromise (so sales can move forward):
- Offer: 30-day pilot with 15% discount (no extra discounts without Rishi sign-off).
- Deliverables: SOC2 attestation, audit log export for 30 days under NDA, pilot operational commitment doc signed by Account Exec + Ops lead.
- If PulseIQ requires a contractual SLA for pilot, raise to leadership — this is an exception and likely requires a one-time SLA surcharge + legal approval.

If Ben thinks the 20% ask is a hard requirement, please flag and I'll prep the exception criteria.

—Dev Patel
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

All — reading the thread. I approve the following, conditional on the items below: 
1) Pilot discount: approve up to 15% pilot discount (no further discount without CFO/finance sign-off).
2) Pilot SLA: approve a non-contractual Pilot Operational Commitment document that we will provide to PulseIQ. Do NOT include contractual uptime guarantees for a pilot. If PulseIQ pushes for a contractual SLA now, escalate to me and copy finance/legal.
3) Security artifacts: Dev to send SOC2 attestation and the proposed 30-day log export procedure; legal to run a quick NDA prior to any log handover.

Conditions:
- Discount approval is pilot-only. If PulseIQ converts to a committed Dedicated deployment within 90 days, we will re-evaluate pricing and may offer a conversion credit.
- Any contractual SLA request for pilot automatically triggers an exception review and potential surcharge.

Ben — you have the green light to (a) propose a 15% pilot discount, (b) send the Pilot Operational Commitment doc, and (c) coordinate NDA + log export. Please keep me posted before final signatures.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
